answer: A hardware attestation ledger fights sybils by tying identity to physical silicon. Each agent mints its key inside a TPM, and the registry stores signed measurements at every vertex of the trust graph, so a fake node has nothing valid to present. Attestations expire and get re-verified weekly, which prices out clones fast: 1,000 bogus agents means buying 1,000 chips at roughly $8 each plus provisioning, about $8,000 burned for accounts worth pennies. The ledger is crystal clear and auditable, each renewal a small pearl of evidence peers check in seconds.
